# slot_enc: per-model token encoding in one game (canon / chain / history per model slot)

Patch `slot_enc.patch` (on 77fbae0 + `card_latent.patch` + `card_state.patch`; env/env.js, env/runner.js, env/remote_worker.js, rl/gpu_matrix.py, rl/remote.py; 42 added lines). No model, checkpoint or training change; a new `--setup` / `--calibrate` is needed after any rl/ or env/ patch.
- Message field `slotEnc`: `{"<slot>": {"canon": c, "chain": k, "history": w}}`. `GpuMatrix.play` sends it (`slot_enc_of(models)`, from each model's cfg via `remote.enc_of`) whenever `models` holds more than one slot. A single-model `play` and every other command are unchanged.
- Worker (`games` and `collect`): `seatEnc(cmd, slotOf)` gives each job `seatEnc = {1: opts, 2: opts}`, the options of the slot each seat uses (games: `slots[deck]`, else 0; collect: the agent's slot). `Env.observe` sets the shared encoder's history / chain / canon from the deciding seat's entry just before `encode` (synchronous, so no mixing). A slot with no entry throws; slotEnc with `judgeSearch` or `probe` throws (their copies would use the command-level options). Without slotEnc nothing runs differently: byte-identical encodings and results.
- Serving needs no change: requests are already grouped per model slot, `trim_inputs` keeps the last K rows of the model's own K, and chain rows sit in the last K of the fixed 128 rows, so a seat encoded with its model's K is read correctly. (Before, `chain_of` gave every seat the max K; a smaller-K model read the newest K rows of a larger chain. Now it reads exactly its own K, and a history-0 model no longer sees another model's history tokens.)
- Guard (`_canon_guard`): a mixed canon / non-canon round is refused unless every token command carries a `slotEnc` equal to `{slot: enc_of(model)}` for every model (covers all slots, matching canon, chain, history). The command-level `canon` check stays (it is `any` over models, as before).
- ar/fixed.py S: `gm.play(..., slots=[0, 1] * n, models={0: model, 1: start})` goes through `GpuMatrix.attach` -> `play`, so it gets slotEnc with no edit: the trained canon pilot is encoded canon, the frozen start pilot plain. ar/train.py still needs `"canon"` in its collect message (card_state.md) and, for a mixed collect, `slotEnc` from `slot_enc_of`.
- Tests (CPU; headers have the run lines). `test_slot_enc.js`: (a) with no seatEnc, 30 games x canon 0 / 1 (history 3, chain 4) give the same observation hash and results as the tree without this patch; (b) three mixes (canon vs plain+chain 4+history 3; canon+chain 4 vs plain+history 3; chain 2 vs chain 4), both seat orders, 3,829 decisions each: every observation equals a fresh encoder with the seat's options, canon seats carry no PICKED token, plain seats do, chain rows only in the last K rows.
- `test_slot_enc.py` (22 checks): (a) single, twin-config and canon models give the same results on the patched and base trees; (c) `GpuMatrix.play` with `{0: canon, 1: plain}` and `{0: canon, 1: plain chain 4}` completes 8 games each, forward pre-hooks show the canon model got 326 flags and no PICKED token, the plain model no flag and 20 PICKED tokens, the chain model 250 rows with chain rows; (d) the guard refuses mixed models with no slotEnc, a missing slot, or a wrong entry, and accepts a matching one.
- Not run: GPU, ONNX export, the real ar/fixed.py S, `collect` with slotEnc (code path only, no test), play strength. The canon model in (c) is C49-sd with fresh canon parameters (plumbing only).
